subject: Lodestar: request for bespoke uptime remedy and graduated service-credit schedule
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@lodestar.ai>
To: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Kendra Patel <kendra.patel@lodestar.ai>, procurement@lodestar.ai
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: bespoke uptime remedy + tiered service-credit schedule

Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. We’re close on commercials but procurement flagged the standard SLA wording (12x monthly uptime target, fixed service-credit table). For our customers in regulated verticals we need a graduated remedy matrix tied to committed spend tiers (higher commitment => lower relative credits) and a narrower uptime window for which credits apply.

Specifically Lodestar is asking for:
- a 12-month committed annual spend band in the SOW (we can commit to $2.4M/year)
- a graduated credit scale: Tier A (>=$3.0M): max monthly credit 5% of monthly invoice; Tier B ($1.5M–$3.0M): max 10%; Tier C (<$1.5M): 15%
- exclusion for transient throttling events under 20s per request (we can posture that our usage profile is latency-sensitive at the 95th percentile)

We’re happy to accept a modest upcharge or additional commitments on SLAs if you can provide this tailored remedy schedule. Can you route this to the deal desk / leadership for exception? Procurement would like a signed SOW by the end of May.

Attachments: sample_customer_policy.pdf (for context)

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Cloud Partnerships, Lodestar
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: bespoke uptime remedy + tiered service-credit schedule

Forwarding Lodestar’s ask — small enterprise with heavy compliance requirements, possible expansion into gov-adjacent accounts. Procurement deadline end of month. Key points below and my initial read:

- Lodestar proposes a graduated credit schedule tied to committed spend. They’re willing to commit $2.4M/yr today (falls in Tier B under their bands) and would sign 12 months.
- They want tighter exclusions on short throttling spikes (<20s) which we don’t typically carve out explicitly.

Recommended routing to Deal Desk to draft proposed remedy matrix and quantify impact. If we accept a tiered max-credit approach, suggest we:
1) Offer a 3-tier matrix with maximum per-month credits of 5% / 10% / 15% as a starting point, but cap total annual credits to 20% of annual committed spend to protect economics.
2) Require minimum 12-month committed spend and a 90-day notice for downgrades to prevent gaming.
3) Keep exclusions limited to scheduled maintenance and documented platform incidents; do not broadly exclude short tail latency spikes — instead, apply a minimum outage definition (e.g., sustained degraded P50 over 10 mins) to qualify for credits.

Can you Ben / Deal Desk run numbers and escalate for Marissa’s sign-off if necessary? I’ll prep the SOW redline.

—Irene
Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 14:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Deal Desk recommendation: Lodestar LOD-389 — tiered remedy + credit cap

Marissa — Per Irene’s note, attached is a proposed remedy matrix and projected financial exposure (proposed_remedy_matrix.xlsx, sla_history_30d.csv). Summary recommendation:

- Approve a graduated monthly-credit schedule mapped to committed annual spend with the following caps: 
  • Tier A (>= $3.0M): max monthly credit 5%, max annual credits 10% of committed spend
  • Tier B ($1.5M–$3.0M): max monthly credit 10%, max annual credits 15%
  • Tier C (< $1.5M): max monthly credit 15%, max annual credits 20%
- Require a 12-month minimum commitment and 90-day downgrade notice.
- Exclusions: scheduled maintenance and verified third-party outages.
- For transient latency spikes (<30s per event) we recommend not creating an explicit exclusion; instead tie remedies to sustained availability/throughput failures to avoid frequent small claims.

Trade-offs / ask: Lodestar is asking for the original bands shown in their email (5/10/15) and a carve-out for <20s events. I recommend we accept the banding but push the annual cap (as above) and set the minimum incident definition to 10 minutes sustained to qualify for a credit. That limits liability while giving Lodestar the commercial certainty they need.

If you sign off we’ll update the SOW redline and prepare the DocuSign.

—Ben Carter
Head of Deal Desk, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
To: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Deal Desk recommendation: Lodestar LOD-389 — tiered remedy + credit cap

Thanks, Ben. I reviewed the deck and numbers. I approve a one-time exception for Lodestar on the following narrow terms:

- Governance: Exception valid for the initial 12-month SOW only; any renewal requires Deal Desk review.
- Committed spend: Accept their $2.4M/yr commitment in writing (Tier B).
- Remedy matrix (approved): Tier A >=$3.0M (5% monthly / 10% annual), Tier B $1.5M–$3.0M (10% monthly / 15% annual), Tier C < $1.5M (15% monthly / 20% annual).
- Annual credit cap: Hard cap at 15% of committed spend for this initial exception (discount to Ben’s recommended 15%/20% split).
- Incident qualification: Credits only trigger for sustained incidents defined as either (a) availability below 99.5% for a continuous 10-minute window affecting >10% of requests in that window OR (b) system-wide throughput degradation with verified root cause. We will not carve out individual short tail spikes under 30s.
- Require Lodestar to sign the finalized SOW (redline attached) and accept a 90-day downgrade notice.

I’m comfortable approving this because Lodestar is a strategic channel partner and the exposure under these terms is within our modeled bounds. Ben / Jon — proceed to finalize the SOW and finalize the DocuSign link; include the annual cap language and incident qualification verbatim.

—Marissa Cole
VP, Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
From: irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@lodestar.ai>, Kendra Patel <kendra.patel@lodestar.ai>
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Approved: Lodestar bespoke SLA remedy (LOD-389) — next steps and SOW

Alex / Kendra — thank you for the patience. Leadership has approved a one-time, initial-SOW exception with the following confirmed terms (condensed):

- Committed spend: $2.4M for 12 months (Tier B).
- Remedy matrix: Tier A >=$3.0M: 5% monthly / 10% annual; Tier B $1.5M–$3.0M: 10% monthly / 15% annual; Tier C < $1.5M: 15% monthly / 15% annual (annual cap for this SOW is 15% — final clause).
- Incident qualification: Credits only apply for sustained incidents (continuous 10-minute availability drop affecting >10% of requests or verified throughput failures). We will not honor credits for isolated sub-30s latency spikes.
- Operational controls: 90-day downgrade notice; annual cap enforced; renewal requires Deal Desk re-review.

Attached: lodestar_SOW_redline.pdf (redline reflecting the exact SLA language), proposed_remedy_matrix.xlsx, sla_history_30d.csv. Please review the SOW redline and confirm by EOD Thursday so we can issue DocuSign and meet your procurement timeline.

If you’re good, we’ll send the DocuSign link and finalize signatures.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the line.

—Irene Choi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: lodestar_SOW_redline.pdf (redline, 220KB); proposed_remedy_matrix.xlsx (calc); sla_history_30d.csv (export)
